findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed using bare hands to operate faucet handles after completing the handwashing process. The activity was ceased and corrected on site. The employee rewashed hands and used a paper towel to turn off the faucet handles. Ensure that a barrier is used to operate faucet handles after completing the handwashing process to protect against recontamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12(C) Cleaning Procedure. (C) To avoid recontaminating their hands or surrogate prosthetic devices, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a HANDWASHING SINK or the handle of a restroom door.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: The facility is storing cooked egg rolls in a container and is using time control to maintain safety of food, however, an employee was observed bare handing a cooked egg-roll. The activity was ceased and the egg rolls were discarded to correct the violation. Ensure that ready-to-eat (RTE) foods are never handled using bare hands. Instead, use single service gloves or utensils to protect against contamination of food items.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: Thermometers are provided and accurate.
findings.comment: The owners could not locate any probe style thermometers for measuring the internal temperature of foods. The owners mentioned purchasing thermometers as soon as possible. Ensure that probe thermometers are always readily available. Will follow-up on 6/12/2026 to ensure that thermometers have been purchased.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.12 Food Temperature Measuring Devices. (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures as specified under Chapter 3. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small-diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were a couple dead insects observed on the floor underneath a storage rack that stores clean dishes. The dead insects were shown to the PIC and the insects were swept and discarded. The facility contracts with Adam’s Pest Control to provide treatment the building (serviced monthly). Ensure that the premise is cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of unwanted insects.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.112 Removing Dead or Trapped Birds, Insects, Rodents, and Other Pests. Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: An employee was observed rinsing their hands in the triple sink. Discussed with PIC proper handwashing techniques and use of designated handsink. Ensure that handwashing only occurs in sinks designed for handwashing and never ware-washing sinks.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.15 Where to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands in a HANDWASHING SINK or APPROVED automatic handwashing facility and may not clean their hands in a sink used for FOOD preparation or WAREWASHING, or in a service sink or a curbed cleaning facility used for the disposal of mop water and similar liquid waste.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The dish machine repeatedly tested at 0ppm (CL). PIC mentioned that a technician will be contacted later today to service the machine. The facility is instructed to use the triple sink for sanitizing dishes until the dish machine can be serviced. Discussed with facility to routinely check the dish machine’s sanitizer concentration at start of the day to ensure that it is properly sanitizing dishes. A followup to ensure correction of the violation is scheduled for 5/12/2025.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Several dry goods such as but not limited to flours and batter mixes were observed uncovered in the storage closet. The goods were stored in their original packaging but were uncovered and exposed to possible contamination. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that dry goods are always stored in a manner that protected against contamination and never uncovered.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Observed the dish machine to test at 0ppm (CL). Discussed with PIC and technician will be contacted to provide service to the machine. Facility will use the triple sink to sanitize dishes until the dish machine can be serviced. Ensure that the dish machine is functioning properly and testing at 100ppm (CL). 

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: There was observed a bowl stored in the double door glass cooler to be in direct contact with the raw cauliflower stored in a bucket in the cooler. This bowl was removed from this location and placed on the shelf above the cauliflower. Ensure food items are stored in a manner that prevents contamination during storage, preparation, and display. 
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: The facility was observed to be thawing shrimp in the triple sink basin in a container of water without a steady steam of water. During the inspection, the water was turned on to allow a steady stream of water to flow through into the container. Ensure that proepr thawing methods are used when thawing in the facility.
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.11: The hand sink and part of the triple sink are observed to have caulking that is in a state of disrepair. These locations will need to have the current caulking removed and then have a fresh line of caulking placed. Ensure the caulking is repaired in a manner that creates a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easily cleanable surface.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. C

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following locations were observed to have an accumulation of food/soil debris:
-The handle of the standing white freezer
-The inside top shelves of the standing white freezer
-The handle of the standing double door freezer
-The handle of the dish machine
-The right side of the equipment on the cook-line
Ensure these locations are cleaned and sanitized to remove the current buildup of food debris/soil and then are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency necessary o maintain them clean. 
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
The facility was unable to provide verification of food handlers for all employees. By the next routine inspection, ensure all employees in the facility earn their food handlers and have the certificates present in the facility to be verified during inspections.
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was stored incorrectly between use. The mop was found sitting inside the mop sink, which does not allow it to dry properly. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. The mop was moved to an approved position during the inspection. Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment: 4-501.114: Observed the sani buckets in the facility to measure at 0ppm of bleach. Sani buckets must maintain a concentration between 50 and 200ppm to properly sanitize surfaces. The manager was informed, and the sani bucket was changed during the inspection.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil and mold build up on the plastic sheets hanging on the walk in cooler entrance. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text: 6-501.16  (C) Mop was stored incorrectly between use. The mop was found sitting in the top of the mop bucket, which does not allow it to dry properly. Mops shall be placed in a position that allows them to air-dry without soiling walls, equipment, or supplies. The mop was moved to an approved position during the inspection. Reference 6-501.16.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed container of meat in W-I cooler to be under several different foods without cover. Ensure all foods are covered during storage. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: Observed small amount of black mold on ice machine starting to accumulate. Ensure non-food contact surfaces are cleaned as needed. Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment: Observed uncovered containers of flour and peanuts in dry storage area.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C). Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Observed dish machine rinse cycle testing at 0 ppm chlorine.  Data plate on machine calls for 50 ppm chlorine in the rinse cycle.
findings.citation_text: 4-204.117 Warewashing Machines, Automatic Dispensing of Detergents and Sanitizers (Pf).  Reference 3-307.11

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-202.11  (C) Lighting was found not shielded or otherwise protected in the cooking area. Light bulbs shall be shielded, coated, or otherwise shatter-resistant in areas where there is exposed food, clean equipment, utensils, linens; or unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Reference 6-202.11.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
REPEAT> Observed scoop handle to be stored in contact with rice in rice container. All utensils stored  within food must have the handle extended out of food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed dish machine to have 0 ppm chlorine for sanitizer solution. Hot water temperature in dish machine was 145F. Facility was educated that water temperatures too hot can dissipate sanitizer concentration more rapidly. Water heater temperature was turned down and sanitizer concentration was re-checked to be 50 ppm.
750-830 All chemical sanitizers in a dish machine must meet the requirements of 21 CFR 178.1010 to ensure all items are properly sanitized.  Rinse water shall not less than 75F. Provide proper sanitizer concentration.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed numerous chipped dishes throughout. Replace chipped dishes to provide smooth and easily cleanable food contact surfaces.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak at the 3 compartment sink. Repair leak.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: CORRECTED> Observed the floor under/behind the ice machine to be soiled. Clean floor.
findings.citation_text: 750.1220 Floors shall be kept free of accumulated soil, dirt and food debris.

findings.title: Wholesome, sound condition
findings.comment:
CORRECTED > Observed four cans in the dry storage area to have denting along the top and/or bottoms seams. Cans were segregated and held on to for return credit.
750-100 Food shall be in sound condition, free from spoilage, filth, and other contamination and shall be safe for human consumption.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
REPEAT > Observed liquids on the wok line to be out of original container and not labeled with product common name. Label all liquids and powders out of original containers.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed food to be inproperly stored in the following areas. 1) Chicken stored on floor of walk-in. 2) Personal food stored above food for service in the white combo fridge. 3) Food in walk-in uncovered. 4) Food in prep cooler uncovered. 5) Powders and sauces on the wok line uncovered. Store all food properly.
750-120(a) Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.
750-130(b) Food shall be stored at least 6 inches off the floor.  Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled REPEAT > 1) Interior of the microwave including the ceiling. Wash, rInse, and sanitize al food contact surfaces.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) The chemical storage shelf under the dish table. 2) The magnetic knife holder in the dish area. 3) The wok table. 4) all rooling carts in the kitchen. 5) The exterior sides of the fryer and oven. 6) Interior of cook line freezer. 7) Interior of silver meat freezer. 8) Interior of reach in freezer. 9) Exterior of the microwave. 10) Exterior of all bulk food containers. Clean all non-food contact surfaces.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
Observed dishes on the cook prep table and server counter to be stored with food-contact side exposed. Invert or cover dishes to protect them from contamination.
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service bowls being stored in the kitchen with food contact surface exposed. Invert or cover items to protect them from contamination.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the floors to be soiled throughout the facility under equipment, tables, coolers, and along walls in the kitchen, dish area, dry storage area, mop sink room, and in the walk-in cooler. Clean all flooring.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
Observed the urinal in the mens room to not be sealed to the wall. Seal urinal to wall.
750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed two mops stored with heads on ground. Store mops so head can easily air dry.
750-1390 Maintenance and cleaning tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners and similiar equipment shall be maintained and stored in a way that does not contaminate food.
